Since it is currently April 21, 2026, you are just a few days past the April 15 deadline for your 2025 tax year filing. It's a stressful spot to be in, but the best move is to act quickly to minimize any potential penalties.

How to Find Your 2024 Tax Return

Since you normally use TurboTax, your 2024 return (the one you filed last year) should be stored in your account or on your device:

  • If you used TurboTax Online:
    1. Sign in to your TurboTax account.
    2. On the Tax Home screen, scroll down to the section labeled Your tax returns & documents.
    3. Select 2024 from the list.
    4. Click Download/print return (PDF) to save a copy.
  • If you used the TurboTax Desktop software:
    1. Search your computer for files ending in .tax2024.
    2. By default, these are saved in your Documents > TurboTax folder.
  • If you can't find it:
    • Check if you might have used a different email address or user ID. TurboTax has an account recovery tool if you think you have multiple accounts.

What to Do About Being Late (2025 Taxes)

Because the April 15 deadline has passed, you can no longer file for an automatic extension (the request itself was due on the 15th). Here is how to handle the "few days late" situation:

  • File Immediately: The IRS calculates penalties based on how late you are. A "failure to file" penalty is much higher (usually 5% of the unpaid taxes per month) than a "failure to pay" penalty (0.5% per month). Filing today stops that 5% clock from ticking further.
  • Check Your Refund Status: If you are actually owed a refund, there is typically no penalty for filing late. The penalties only apply if you owe the IRS money.
  • Pay What You Can: If you owe money and can't pay the full amount right now, file the return anyway and pay whatever you can. This reduces the interest and late-payment penalties.
  • Contractor/LLC Considerations: Since you are doing independent contract work and managing an LLC, you likely need to account for self-employment taxes. Even if your records aren't perfect, it's often better to file an estimated return now and amend it later once you find your 2024 data for comparison.

Next Steps

  1. Log in to TurboTax right now to see if you can pull that 2024 PDF.
  2. Start your 2025 return immediately. TurboTax can often "pull in" your data from the previous year automatically if you use the same account, which might save you from needing the 2024 physical document right this second.
